Each insert is shown exactly as appended after the task. Blue lines are statement headers ([id; kind; basis; threat; catalogue ids]); highlighted lines are the failure-behaviour clauses; grey lines are anchors and verification hints. Counts beside each insert are the round's own: functional artifacts of N, and issue checks failed / unresolved / passed of 10N, for the arms that received the insert and for the round's fresh control.

Agent instruction versions. v7 and v8 (rounds I10 to I18): no rule about failure behaviour. v9 (I19) adds rule 6:

6. Fail safe without losing the change's effect. Rejection belongs at the boundary where untrusted data enters (parser, decoder, store). At the integration point where the change produces its primary effect, a missing or invalid value is substituted by a stated default or normalized so that the effect still occurs; never propose skipping or suppressing the primary effect as failure behavior.

v10 (I20, I21a, I21b) replaces it with:

6. Fail safe without losing the change's effect. The operation that receives untrusted data (parser, decoder, store) rejects invalid input and reports the rejection; it never substitutes or clamps. The caller at the integration point, where the change produces its primary effect, substitutes a stated default or normalizes a missing or invalid value before it calls that operation, so the effect still occurs; never propose skipping or suppressing the primary effect as failure behavior.

Task-relevant security context for adding persistent highscores to ApoMario. The game exposes the active level through the component and exposes level players; player points are mutable and level completion updates points before/around end-of-run processing. The level also exposes a remaining-time value and a passed-time calculation, but the inspected code does not establish that either is elapsed wall-clock milliseconds. Menu architecture is model/panel based and uses a navigation graph, so a dedicated highscore view must cross the existing menu navigation/rendering boundary. No remote calls or cryptographic mechanisms were observed in the inspected excerpts. Persistence is a new local file boundary supplied by the required Path constructor; its location, format, permissions, corruption handling, and atomicity remain implementation decisions and were not established by the snapshot.


 


[security_property; observed; active-level and player trust boundary] ApoMarioComponent owns the current ApoMarioLevel and provides getLevel/setLevel; ApoMarioLevel provides getPlayers(), making the level object the integration boundary for obtaining run state.


Task relevance: recordRunEnd(level) must derive data from the supplied level rather than a separate or stale score source.

Security context for the requested highscore feature: ApoIcarus provides a singleton in-memory highscore with parallel name/time/points lists and network POST/GET persistence. ApoMario's indexed source has no inspected highscore implementation or matching search hits. ApoMarioLevel owns level time and player state; player points are mutable and are incremented for coins and finish outcomes, so run-end recording must occur after the terminal scoring logic and before the level/player state is discarded. The required integration must add a file-backed board, a dedicated menu view/panel, and a call at both clearing and losing terminal paths. Storage input is a file Path and player name is user-controlled; persistence and rendering should treat both as untrusted data. Preserve list alignment, validate decoded record counts/types/ranges, bound file size and record count, use safe character/length handling for names, avoid remote/network submission, and use atomic replacement or otherwise failure-safe writes. Survival time is required in milliseconds and only formatted as mm:ss at display time; avoid integer overflow when converting or calculating elapsed duration. The target repository is an indexed JAR snapshot, so edits to embedded source may require corresponding build/source integration not visible in the snapshot.

Security context for the requested highscore feature: ApoIcarus provides a singleton in-memory highscore with parallel name/time/points lists and network POST/GET persistence. Its save path URL-encodes the score, time, and player name but sends them to a remote endpoint; its load path parses an unbounded line stream in repeating point/time/name groups directly into integer lists. ApoMario's indexed source has no inspected highscore implementation or matching search hits. ApoMarioLevel owns level time and player state; player points are mutable and are incremented for coins and finish outcomes, so run-end recording must occur after the terminal scoring logic and before the level/player state is discarded. The required integration must add a file-backed board, a dedicated menu view/panel, and a call at both clearing and losing terminal paths. Storage input is a file Path and player name is user-controlled; persistence and rendering should treat both as untrusted data. Preserve list alignment, validate decoded record counts/types/ranges, bound file size and record count, use safe character/length handling for names, avoid remote/network submission, and use atomic replacement or otherwise failure-safe writes. Survival time is required in milliseconds and only formatted as mm:ss at display time; avoid integer overflow when converting or calculating elapsed duration. The target repository is an indexed JAR snapshot, so edits to embedded source may require corresponding build/source integration not visible in the snapshot.

Security context for the requested highscore feature: ApoIcarus provides a singleton in-memory highscore with parallel name/time/points lists and network POST/GET persistence. Its save path URL-encodes the score, time, and player name but sends them to a remote endpoint; its load path parses an unbounded line stream in repeating point/time/name groups directly into integer lists. ApoMario's indexed source has no inspected highscore implementation or matching search hits. ApoMarioLevel owns level time and player state; player points are mutable and are incremented for coins and finish outcomes, so run-end recording must occur after the terminal scoring logic and before the level/player state is discarded. The required integration must add a file-backed board, a dedicated menu view/panel, and a call at both clearing and losing terminal paths. Storage input is a file Path and player name is user-controlled; persistence and rendering should treat both as untrusted data. Preserve list alignment, validate decoded record counts/types/ranges, bound file size and record count, use safe character/length handling for names, avoid remote/network submission, and use atomic replacement or otherwise failure-safe writes. Survival time is required in milliseconds and only formatted as mm:ss at display time; avoid integer overflow when converting or calculating elapsed duration. The target repository is an indexed JAR snapshot, so edits to embedded source may require corresponding build/source integration not visible in the snapshot.

Security context for the requested highscore feature: ApoIcarus provides a singleton in-memory highscore with parallel name/time/points lists and network POST/GET persistence. ApoMario's indexed source has no inspected highscore implementation or matching search hits. ApoMarioLevel owns level time and player state; player points are mutable and are incremented for coins and finish outcomes, so run-end recording must occur after the terminal scoring logic and before the level/player state is discarded. The required integration must add a file-backed board, a dedicated menu view/panel, and a call at both clearing and losing terminal paths. Storage input is a file Path and player name is user-controlled; persistence and rendering should treat both as untrusted data. Preserve list alignment, validate decoded record counts/types/ranges, bound file size and record count, use safe character/length handling for names, avoid remote/network submission, and use atomic replacement or otherwise failure-safe writes. Survival time is required in milliseconds and only formatted as mm:ss at display time; avoid integer overflow when converting or calculating elapsed duration. The target repository is an indexed JAR snapshot, so edits to embedded source may require corresponding build/source integration not visible in the snapshot.

ApoMario currently computes player points and run completion in ApoMarioLevel#setAnalysis, exposes player names/points and elapsed-time state through ApoMarioLevel, initializes menu/game panels in ApoMarioPanel, and renders menu player data in ApoMarioMenu. Existing file-backed level/replay/property loading accepts local file data at several boundaries. The requested highscore feature introduces a new local persistence store, run-end recording flow, and dedicated menu view; those new operations are not present in the inspected source.

ApoIcarus provides reusable highscore storage and rendering patterns, but its storage is network-oriented and parses unvalidated integers. ApoMario already exposes terminal score/time state through ApoMarioLevel and player state, and routes both completion and loss through setAnalysis(boolean). The proposed feature should add a bounded, validated local-file store, record the terminal player state exactly once before analysis navigation, and add a menu panel rendering aligned records sorted by descending score.

      ApoIcarus provides reusable highscore storage and rendering patterns, but its storage is network-oriented and parses unvalidated integers. ApoMario already exposes terminal score/time state through ApoMarioLevel and player state, and routes both completion and loss through setAnalysis(boolean). The proposed feature should add a bounded, validated local-file store, record the terminal player state exactly once before analysis navigation, and add a menu panel rendering aligned records sorted by descending score.

                    High-level guidance for adding gameplay achievements with per-run evaluation, cross-session persistence, and a dedicated menu view.
                    

                     
                    

                    Assets:
                    

                    - Achievement unlock state [integrity]
                    

                    - Per-run achievement measurements [integrity]
                    

                    - Achievements menu panel [availability]
                    

                     
                    

                    Trust boundaries:
                    

                    - Achievement persistence [entry point]: Locally editable achievement store contents from Desktop filesystem to Achievement state loader
                    

                    - Level-derived run results [entry point]: Values and entities from local or shared level content from Level file or level server to Finished-run achievement evaluator
                    

                    - Gameplay and menu interaction [entry point]: Local tampering with gameplay state or menu inputs from Desktop game process and user-controlled files to Achievement counters, unlock decisions, and panel display
                    

                     
                    

                    [X1; change_risk; reasoned; tampering; CWE-20; CAPEC-153] Achievement state could be forged or corrupted if persisted identifiers and values are trusted without validation.
                    

                    Task relevance: Cross-session unlock progress must remain meaningful despite editable local files.
                    

                    Basis: prospective task requirement or reasoning; not an implemented safeguard.
                    

                    Relations: related R1
                    

                     
                    

                    [X2; change_risk; reasoned; elevation_of_privilege; CWE-602] Run progress could leak across runs or be awarded from manipulated level data if counters and final evaluation are not separated from persistent unlock state.
                    

                    Task relevance: Each achievement must use actual values from one completed run while unlocked achievements persist.
                    

                    Basis: prospective task requirement or reasoning; not an implemented safeguard.
                    

                    Relations: related R2, related R3
                    

                     
                    

                    [X3; change_risk; reasoned; denial_of_service; CWE-400] Malformed persistence data or unbounded achievement display data could prevent the game or menu from functioning.
                    

                    Task relevance: The feature must remain usable when local storage is missing, damaged, or oversized.
                    

                    Basis: prospective task requirement or reasoning; not an implemented safeguard.
                    

                    Relations: related R4, related R5
                    

                     
                    

                    [R1; requirement; task; tampering; CWE-20; CAPEC-153] At the operation that receives persisted achievement data, accept only the three known nonblank identifiers POINTS_GOAL, ENEMIES_GOAL, and TIME_GOAL, and retain at most three records with identifiers of at most 32 characters.
                    

                    Task relevance: Prevents local store tampering from creating arbitrary unlocks or excessive retained state.
                    

                    Failure behavior: Invalid records are rejected and reported; the caller uses an empty achievement set so gameplay and the menu still operate.
                    

                    Basis: prospective task requirement or reasoning; not an implemented safeguard.
                    

                    Relations: mitigates X1
                    

                     
                    

                    [R2; requirement; task; elevation_of_privilege; CWE-284] At the start of every run, reset points, enemy-kill count, and survived time to zero while leaving the cross-session unlocked set unchanged.
                    

                    Task relevance: Ensures progress does not carry across runs while previously unlocked achievements remain available.
                    

                    Failure behavior: A run with missing or invalid initial values starts from zero rather than inheriting prior progress.
                    

                    Basis: prospective task requirement or reasoning; not an implemented safeguard.
                    

                    Relations: mitigates X2
                    

                     
                    

                    [R3; requirement; task; elevation_of_privilege; CWE-602] At the gameplay integration point, evaluate POINTS_GOAL at 20,000 non-negative points, ENEMIES_GOAL at three or more non-negative kills, and TIME_GOAL strictly above 60,000 non-negative milliseconds, using the finished level's actual run values and unlocking each goal as soon as its threshold is reached.
                    

                    Task relevance: Makes unlocks originate from real gameplay and preserves the exact threshold semantics.
                    

                    Failure behavior: Missing or invalid gameplay measurements are normalized to zero before evaluation; no achievement is awarded for an invalid threshold value.
                    

                    Basis: prospective task requirement or reasoning; not an implemented safeguard.

                    [R4; requirement; reasoned; denial_of_service; CWE-400] At the persistence read operation, read no more than 4,096 bytes total, no more than 128 characters per line, and no more than 32 characters per field before retaining data.

                    Basis: prospective task requirement or reasoning; not an implemented safeguard.

                                    --- BEGIN REPOSITORY-DERIVED SECURITY CONTEXT (angle: requirements) ---
                                    

                                    Generic security context for a Java desktop game's achievement tracking, local persistence, and menu display. No repository was available for inspection.
                                    

                                     
                                    

                                    Assets:
                                    

                                    - Achievement records [integrity]
                                    

                                    - Game availability [availability]
                                    

                                    - Achievement data handling [resistance]
                                    

                                     
                                    

                                    Trust boundaries:
                                    

                                    - Running-game progress [entry point]: Points, enemy counts, and survival durations produced or tampered with during gameplay from Running game state and local cheating attempts to Achievement progress and unlock evaluation
                                    

                                    - Local achievement store [entry point]: User-editable persisted achievement records and file contents from Local filesystem to Achievement store parser and loader
                                    

                                    - External level content [entry point]: Level data loaded from a shared level server or other external source from Outside the program to Level parser and gameplay integration
                                    

                                     
                                    

                                    [R1; requirement; task; tampering; CWE-20; CAPEC-20] The operation that receives achievement progress or run-finalization values shall accept only non-negative integers for points, enemy counts, and elapsed milliseconds, and shall reject and report values outside that domain without substituting or clamping them.
                                    

                                    Task relevance: Protects threshold evaluation from malformed or tampered gameplay inputs.
                                    

                                    Failure behavior: Reject and report the invalid value; the gameplay integration caller shall normalize missing or invalid progress to the stated non-negative default before invoking the operation so gameplay achievement tracking continues.
                                    

                                    Basis: prospective task requirement or reasoning; not an implemented safeguard.
                                    

                                     
                                    

                                    [R2; requirement; reasoned; denial_of_service; CWE-400; CWE-789; CAPEC-130] The achievement store shall read untrusted files using bounded units: no more than 64 KiB per line, 256 KiB per record, and 1 MiB total per store read; data exceeding a bound shall be rejected and reported.
                                    

                                    Task relevance: Prevents oversized local files from exhausting memory or blocking startup.
                                    

                                    Failure behavior: The parser rejects and reports the oversized unit; the loading caller uses an empty achievement set before calling the parser so the game and achievement feature remain available.
                                    

                                    Basis: prospective task requirement or reasoning; not an implemented safeguard.
                                    

                                     
                                    

                                    [R3; requirement; reasoned; elevation_of_privilege; CWE-502; CWE-913; CAPEC-586] The persisted achievement format shall be explicit data such as bounded text or structured records and shall not use Java object deserialization or execute code represented by store contents.
                                    

                                    Task relevance: Ensures saved achievement records cannot trigger code execution when loaded.
                                    

                                    Failure behavior: The receiving decoder rejects and reports unsupported executable or serialized input; the caller initializes an empty achievement set before decoding so normal gameplay and unlocking still work.
                                    

                                    Basis: prospective task requirement or reasoning; not an implemented safeguard.
                                    

                                     
                                    

                                    [R4; requirement; task; denial_of_service; CWE-248; CWE-703; CAPEC-吹] Malformed, unreadable, or semantically invalid achievement-store contents shall not prevent the game or menu from running; the load integration point shall substitute an empty unlocked-achievement set before requesting parsing or display.
                                    

                                    Task relevance: Preserves availability while allowing achievements to unlock and be saved after recovery.
                                    

                                    Failure behavior: The store operation rejects and reports the malformed input, while its caller uses the empty set and continues the primary game/menu operation.
                                    

                                    Basis: prospective task requirement or reasoning; not an implemented safeguard.
                                    

                                     
                                    

                                    [R5; requirement; reasoned; denial_of_service; CWE-400; CAPEC-130] The retained unlocked-achievement collection shall be bounded to the three defined achievement identifiers, and any additional records shall be evicted or omitted from retained and displayed state rather than causing an otherwise valid defined achievement to be rejected.
                                    

                                    Task relevance: Keeps persistence and the dedicated menu panel small and predictable.
                                    

                                    Failure behavior: The collection bounds operation evicts unsupported excess records and reports the condition; the caller retains the valid defined achievements and continues displaying the panel.
                                    

                                    Basis: prospective task requirement or reasoning; not an implemented safeguard.
